full_judgment: 2. The circumstances taken into consideration in those judgments may be briefly outlined as follows. Mst. Khairunnessa, predecessor of the respondents as plaintiff brought the suit for khas possession of the disputed property asserting her title and defendant No. 1 resisted it. The plaintiff examined three witnesses and provided several documents in support of her claim. The defendant in spite of several dates failed to cross-examine the witnesses, besides PW 1. She did not depose herself on commission or even deposit the commission fees. The trial Court fixed 10 March 1993 for argument of the case when the defendant filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for an opportunity to cross-examine PW 2 and PW 3 and issue summons upon witnesses. The trial Court allowed the application and observed that the witnesses for cross-examination were present in court and the defendant had liberty to cross-examine them. But the lawyer of the defendant was not available for the purpose. The court heard the argument and delivered the judgment on 16 March 1993 decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff. It was from this judgment that the defendant preferred First Appeal No. 79 of 1993 giving rise to Civil Appeal No. 63 of 1995.
